# PyAutoFit Assistant

> The front door of the PyAutoFit Assistant — an AI assistant for statistical inference in your own scientific domain: agent instructions, task skills and a reference wiki in one repository that you drive in natural language from inside an AI coding agent. It routes by intent: set up, see what the assistant can do, read the reference, or jump to runnable examples.

## How to use it

The assistant is supported **only inside an AI coding agent** that can read this repository and execute Python: **Claude Code** or **Codex** (recommended and tested), or **OpenCode** as an experimental alternative. Clone the repository and open the agent inside it — `AGENTS.md` (via `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code) loads automatically:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autofit_assistant.git
cd autofit_assistant
claude        # or: codex / opencode
```

Then paste the starting prompt from the [README](./README.md) (or its "Bring Your Own Likelihood" prompt). Setup pages: [`docs/setup/claude_code.md`](./docs/setup/claude_code.md) · [`docs/setup/codex_cli.md`](./docs/setup/codex_cli.md) · [`docs/setup/opencode_cli.md`](./docs/setup/opencode_cli.md). Desktop and IDE versions of these agents are fine when they provide the same repository and execution access. Browser chats with a GitHub connector are **no longer supported** (retired 2026-09-10; see [`docs/archive/`](./docs/archive/README.md)).

Agentic does not mean autonomous: you can discuss a model, choose priors, plan an analysis or learn in **Teacher Mode** without running anything — say so in your prompt.

## If you are an agent reading this file

Read order: [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md) → [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md) → the relevant skill → [wiki/](./wiki). Never write PyAutoFit from memory: mirror the matching skill's calls and verify symbols against the installed library (`dir()`, or `python autoassistant/audit_skill_apis.py --code "<snippet>"` on a harness without the PreToolUse code gate). Inspect the user's data (plot it, or print a numerical summary) before composing any fit, and never silently alter the user's likelihood code.

## Agent instructions (canonical)

- [AGENTS.md](./AGENTS.md): safety rules, modes, domain adaptation, and repository conventions — the source of truth.

## What it can do

- [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md): one-line index of every task skill. The
  defining ones: wrap your likelihood code, ingest your field's papers, adapt to your
  domain.

## Reference

- [wiki/core/index.md](./wiki/core/index.md): curated PyAutoFit + statistics reference — stack, inference concepts (priors, samplers, evidence, EP), operations.
- [wiki/literature/index.md](./wiki/literature/index.md): *your* domain's science wiki — ships near-empty by design and grows as you ingest your field's papers.

## Runnable examples & tutorials (elsewhere)

- [autofit_workspace](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/autofit_workspace): end-to-end example scripts, cookbooks and notebooks.
- [HowToFit](https://github.com/PyAutoLabs/HowToFit): from-first-principles model-fitting lecture series.
